DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 80 s. 2021 JUN 18 2021 HON. SEBASTIAN M. PUACHE Municipal Vice Mayor Municipality of Unisan, Quezon Dear Vice Mayor Puache: This has reference to your letter dated 22 March 2021, requesting this Department's legal opinion regarding the following: a. What can the Sangguniang Bayan of Unisan, Quezon do regarding the plan of their Municipal Mayor Ferdinand P. Adulta to convert their town plaza, Tamesis Park, into a multi-purpose building/Evacuation Center even if this is against the guidance of the National Historic Commission of the Philippines? b. What is the authority of the Municipal Mayor to lend a property of the LGU to a private group without authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan? c. Can the Sangguniang Bayan approve the request for transfer of custodial and maintenance activities of the Remedios Etorma Suarez Memorial Auditorium from their LGU to the Congressional District Office of the 3rd District Representative? Per the documents received by the Central Office, the following are the facts stated: With respect to the first query, the original plan as regards Tamesis Plaza is to install a simple roof, wherein a specific budget has been allotted. However, you and the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) were informed that Mayor Ferdinand P. Adulta (Mayor Adulta) was able to secure assistance from PAGCOR which facilitated the subject changes in the plan. Hence, from the original plan of installing a roof, the same has been altered into a multi-purpose building/evacuation center. The foregoing change in the plan was not agreed by the SB. By reason thereof, the guidance and position of the National Historical

Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) has been sought. As response thereto, NHCP furnished the Office of the SB a copy of NHCP Resolution No. 7, Series of 2018 which declares that Spanish and American colonial period plazas and public squares are national historical sites. Consequently, on 23 October 2020, NHCP, through Dr. Rene R. Escalante, Chairman, advised the SB not to undertake any work or changes in the area and to coordinate with their office. In view of the position given by NHCP, the SB wrote Mayor Adulta requesting him to defer the project, and to ensure that the historical value of the Tamesis Park is protected, as well as to consult the NHCP for the design of the said project, but to no avail. In fact, the SB and Vice Mayor Puache were informed of the continuance of the project. • With respect to the second query, a complaint was filed by Hon. Cristina Caper, Punong Barangay of Barangay F. De Jesus, regarding the permission given by Mayor Adulta in favor of 4K Women's Organization to use the TESDA training building as their office. The matter was endorsed to the Office of the Mayor, wherein it was clarified by Mayor Adulta, in a letter dated 16 November 20202, that it is his own private women's organization (KAMPI), and not the 4K Women's Organization, that he gave his permission to- Contrarily, it is the view of Vice Mayor Puache and the SB that all LGU properties may be used by private individuals/organizations if allowed by legislation or through a Memorandum of Agreement approved by the sanggunian. • With respect to the third query, the Office of the SB received a letter dated 06 July 2020 from the office of the 3rd District Congressional Representative, requesting the SB to return the "custodial and maintenance activities of RESMA" to the office of 3rd District Congressional Representative to be shared by the Office of Barangay F. De Jesus. Hence, the foregoing queries. Propriety of Converting Tamesis into Multi-Purpose Park Building/Evacuation Center

This Department duly acknowledges the position of the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) regarding the matter, being the primary government agency responsible for the promotion of Philippine history, and mandated to undertake and prescribe the manner of restoration, conservation, and protection of the country's historical properties. Nonetheless, may we note that Section 1 1 (c) of Republic Act No. 71601 otherwise known as the "Local Govemment Code of 1991" (LGC), states that local government offices and facilities shall not be transferred, relocated, or converted to other uses unless public hearing are first conducted for the purpose and the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the sanggunian concerned is obtained. In relation thereto, one of the duties of the SB is to regulate the use of public places and approve the construction, improvement, repair and maintenance of the same2. Hence, even if the NHCP allows the conversion of the town plaza into a multi-purpose building, concurrence of the Sangguniang Bayan of Unisan is still required. Accordingly, we find no reason to deviate, and we hereby concur to the position of NHCP. Authority of the Municipal Mayor to Lend a Property of the LGU to a Private Group without the from Authorization Sanqquniang Bayan May we note that Section 22(c) of the LGC in relation to 444(b)(1 )(vi)3 and Section 447(2)(v) of the same Code, provides for the local government 1 SECTION 22. corporate Powers. (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local governrnent unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concemed. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. 2 Section 447(5)(v) 3 SECTION 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation — (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall:

unit's (LGU's) power to enter into contracts on behalf of the LGU upon authorization of the sangguniang bayan. In connection therewith, Section 36 of the same Code, which states: "SECTION 36. Assistance to People's and Non-govemmental Organizations. — A local government unit may, through its local chief executive and with the concurrence of the sanqqunian concemed provide assistance, financial or otherwise, to such people's and non-govemmental organizations for economic, socially-oriented, environmental, or cultural projects to be implemented within its territorial jurisdiction." (Emphasis and Underscoring Supplied) Clearly, based on the foregoing, LGUs may provide assistance to organizations, such as KAMP', in the form of financial assistance or otherwise, subject however to the concurrence of the sanggunian concerned. In such case, should there be a contract for that purpose, the local chief executive (LCE) concemed should first obtain authorization from the sanggunian to enter into contract with the organization. In sum, on the premise that the T ESDA training building is owned by the LGU, the same can be leased or utilize by private parties/organization, provided the same is with the concurrence and approval of the sangguniang bayan. Lastly, the duty of the Municipal Mayor to allocate and assign office space is specifically provided in Section 444(b)(1 )(ix) of the LGC, which states: SECTION 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — (b) For efficient, effective and economical govemance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal govemment, and in this connection, shall: (ix) Allocate and assign office space to municipal and other officials and employees who, bv law or ordinance. are entitled to such space in (he (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: (vi) Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance;

municipal hall and other buildinqs owned or leased by the municipal govemment; (Underscoring supplied) Transfer of "Custodial and Maintenance Activities" of the Remedios Etorma Suarez Memorial Auditorium (RESMA) from the LGU of Unisan to the Congressional District Office of the 3rd District Representative Please be advised that this level cannot squarely answer the last query since the facts provided lacks information necessary for us to deduce an accurate response (e.g. reason for the transfer of custody; source of funds for the construction of RESMA). Nonetheless, we shall answer the same in its general sense. Pertinent to herein discussion are Sections 3754, 3765, 3776, 381 of the LGC, which pertain to the accountability, responsibility, and measure of liability with respect to government properties. 4 SECTION 375. Primary and Secondary Accountability for Government Property. — (a) Each head of department or office of a province. city. municipality or barangay shall be primarily accountable for all government property assigned or issued to his department or office. The person or persons entrusted with the possession or custody of government property under the accountability of any head of department or office shall be immediately accountable to such officer. (b) The head of a department or office primarily accountable for govemment property may require any person in possession of the property or having custody and control thereof under him to keep such records and make reports as may be necessary for his own information and protection. (c) Buildings and other physical structures shall be under the accountability and responsibility of the provincial or city general services officer or the municipal mayor or punong barangay, as the case may (d) Every officer primarily accountable for government property Shall keep a complete record of all properties under his charge and render his accounts therefor semiannually to the provincial or city general services officer or the municipal mayor or punong barangay, as the case may be. s SECTION 376. Responsibility for Proper Use and Care of Government Property. — The person in actual physical possession of government property or entrusted with its custody and control shall be responsible for its proper use and care and shall exercise due diligence in the utilization and safekeeping thereof. 6 SECTION 377. Measure of Liability of Persons Accountable for Government Property. — (a) The person immediately accountable for government property shall be liable for its money value in case of the illegal, improper or unauthorized use or misapplication thereof, by himself or any other person for whose acts he may be responsible, and he shall be liable for all loss, damage, or deterioration occasioned by negligence in the keeping or use of such property unless it is proved that he has exercised due diligence and care in the utilization and safekeeping thereof

In sum, the aforesaid provision provides that each head of department or office of a province, city, municipality or barangay shall be primarily accountable for all govemment property assigned or issued to his department or office. In case a person/s has been entrusted with the possession or custody of the same, he/she shall be immediately accountable to such officer. However, buildings and other physical structures shall be under the accountability and responsibility of the provincial or city general services officer or the municipal mayor or punong barangay, as the case may be. Despite the foregoing, a property which has become unserviceable or is no longer needed may be transferred without cost to another office, agency, subdivision or instrumentality of the national government or another local government unit at an appraised valuation determined by the local Committee on Awards. Such transfer shall be subject to the approval of the sanggunian concemed making the transfer and by the head of the office, agency, subdivision, instrumentality or local government unit receiving the property7 This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARL RINGAN Unde retary for Local Govemment Legal/91 Copy Furnished: Regional Director Ariel O. (c) In cases of loss, damage, or deterioration of govemment property arising from, or attributable to, negligence in security, the head of the security agency shall be held liable therefor. 7 SECTION 381, LGC
